tool_arguments.query: Marvell Technology data center revenue Q3 fiscal 2026

events.content: Marvell Technology data center revenue Q3 fiscal 2026

Marvell generated **$1.518 billion of data-center revenue in Q3 fiscal 2026** (three months ended **November 1, 2025**), up **38% year over year** from $1.101 billion and **2% sequentially** from $1.491 billion. [[1]] 

Data center represented **73% of Marvell’s $2.075 billion total Q3 revenue**, making it the company’s dominant end market. [[1]] 

The quarterly increase was approximately **$27.4 million sequentially**, while the year-over-year increase was approximately **$416.8 million**, based on Marvell’s reported end-market revenue figures. [[1]] 

Marvell does **not** disclose separate Q3 revenue amounts for **custom AI silicon** versus **electro-optics**; it reports their contribution within the aggregate data-center end market rather than as standalone product-revenue lines. [[1]] 

Management had identified strong AI demand for both custom silicon and electro-optics as a key growth driver entering Q3, and stated that custom-AI design activity had reached an all-time high, with more than 50 opportunities across over 10 customers. [[2]] 

Total Q3 revenue of **$2.075 billion** exceeded the midpoint of Marvell’s prior **$2.060 billion ±5%** guidance by **$15 million**, while the company guided Q4 fiscal 2026 revenue to **$2.200 billion ±5%**. [[1]] [[2]] [[1]]

Sources:
[S1.1] Marvell Technology, Inc. Reports Third Quarter of Fiscal Year 2026 Financial Results — https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/999/marvell-technology-inc-reports-third-quarter-of-fiscal-year-2026-financial-results

tool_arguments.query: Marvell Technology custom AI silicon revenue fiscal 2026 quarterly

events.content: Marvell Technology custom AI silicon revenue fiscal 2026 quarterly

Marvell did **not publicly report custom AI-silicon revenue as a quarterly standalone line item in fiscal 2026**; it disclosed end-market **data-center revenue** quarterly and later stated that its **custom business generated $1.5 billion for FY2026** (year ended January 31, 2026), approximately double the prior year. [[1]]

| Marvell fiscal 2026 quarter | Quarter end | Data-center revenue | Commentary on custom AI silicon |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Q1 | May 3, 2025 | **$1.441bn** | Management said results and Q2 outlook were driven by the rapid scaling of AI-silicon programs into high-volume production; this is not a separately quantified custom-silicon figure. [[2]]|
| Q2 | Aug. 2, 2025 | **$1.491bn** | Marvell identified strong AI demand for custom silicon and electro-optics as a driver, but did not disclose custom-silicon revenue alone. [[3]]|
| Q3 | Nov. 1, 2025 | Not separately retrieved here | The company reported total revenue of **$2.075bn** and said data-center-product demand drove the quarter; it did not provide a disclosed standalone custom-AI-silicon revenue figure in the cited results. [[4]]|
| Q4 | Jan. 31, 2026 | **$1.650bn** | Management subsequently characterized the full-year custom business as **$1.5bn**, but Q4 custom revenue itself was not separately reported. [[1]]|

For context, total company revenue rose from **$1.895bn in Q1** to **$2.006bn in Q2**, **$2.075bn in Q3**, and **$2.219bn in Q4**; FY2026 revenue was **$8.195bn**. [[5, 3, 4, 6]] 

The key interpretation is that **$1.5bn is a full-year custom-business figure, not a quarterly series**, and it should not be equated with Marvell’s broader data-center revenue because that end market also includes electro-optics and other products. [[1]]

events.content: Marvell Technology electro-optics revenue data center fiscal 2026 quarterly

Marvell does **not** separately disclose quarterly “electro-optics” revenue within its data-center end market; it reports total data-center revenue, while describing electro-optics/optical interconnects as a product-level driver of that revenue. [[1]] [[2]]

| Fiscal 2026 quarter | Data-center revenue |
|---|---:|
| Q1 | **$1,440.6 million** [[3]]|
| Q2 | **$1,490.5 million** [[2]]|
| Q3 | **$1,517.9 million** [[4]]|
| Q4 | **$1,651.3 million** [[4]]|

The four reported quarters total **$6.1003 billion** in FY2026 data-center revenue, consistent with management’s statement that full-year data-center revenue surpassed $6 billion. [[3]] [[2]] [[4]] [[5]] 

Data-center revenue rose sequentially in every FY2026 quarter—approximately **3.5% in Q2, 1.8% in Q3, and 8.8% in Q4**—with Q4 representing **74%** of Marvell’s total revenue. [[2]] [[4]] 

For electro-optics specifically, management attributed Q1 momentum to “robust shipments” of electro-optics products and said Q2 growth was fueled by AI demand for custom silicon and electro-optics, but it did not quantify electro-optics sales as a stand-alone quarterly revenue line. [[3]] [[2]]
